## Run it

TRIALMON is an R Shiny app on synthetic data. From the repository root:

```r
install.packages(c("shiny", "bslib", "DT", "ggplot2"))   # once
shiny::runApp("sasr_monitoring_wiki/trialmon_shiny")
```

The console opens on the ranked worklist. Click a point on the eDISH plot, or a participant row in
the worklist, to open that participant's packet in the sidebar. The SAP settings in the sidebar switch
the CTCAE version (v6.0 or v5.0), the potential Hy's Law window and the optional ALP convention, and
every panel re-computes. The study tier has a what-if: pick an indicator, set its level, and watch the
tiers re-roll worst-of. The worklist download is a CSV built in the browser; its file name starts with
SYNTHETIC and its first column says the data are synthetic.

**Shinylive build.** It is also exported as a Shinylive build: [open it in your
browser](../../apps/trialmon/) (smoke-tested in headless Chrome before each deploy, [run
history](https://github.com/patrickiben/biometrics-ai-portfolio/actions/workflows/pages.yml); Shinylive and webR, so R starts in the browser, the first visit downloads about 65 MB,
and it works best in Chrome or Edge; Safari support may vary). The app needed no changes
for that: its data sit inside the app folder, it uses only shiny, bslib and DT (the plots are base graphics), and the
download goes through `session$sendCustomMessage()` and a few lines of JavaScript that save a Blob,
because a `downloadHandler` needs a server. The site's Pages workflow (`.github/workflows/pages.yml`)
exports it with the shinylive R package 0.5.0 (assets 0.10.12), and a local export gave the same
tiers, counts and download in headless Chrome as the native app.

The files, shown in full below:

- **trialmon_shiny/R/logic.R**: the screening rules in base R, no Shiny. The [guide](trialmon-guide.html), the [snapshot](trialmon-dashboard.html), the [SRC packet](trialmon-src-packet.html) and the tests call these functions.
- **trialmon_shiny/R/gen_data.R**: writes the synthetic ADaM-shaped CSVs from one seed.
- **trialmon_shiny/app.R**: the UI and the reactive server.
- **trialmon_tests/**: testthat tests for the rule boundaries, the shipped study and the server.

## The data it reads

Seven CSVs in `trialmon_shiny/data/`, all synthetic: [`adsl`](../trialmon_shiny/data/adsl.csv) (one row
per participant: cohort, dose, disposition, DLT status), [`adlb`](../trialmon_shiny/data/adlb.csv)
(chemistry and hematology by visit, with ANRLO, ANRHI and BASE), [`adeg`](../trialmon_shiny/data/adeg.csv)
(QTcF by visit and time point), [`adae`](../trialmon_shiny/data/adae.csv) (MedDRA preferred term and
primary SOC, grade, seriousness), [`cohorts`](../trialmon_shiny/data/cohorts.csv),
[`study_kri`](../trialmon_shiny/data/study_kri.csv) (operational study-level indicators) and
[`notes`](../trialmon_shiny/data/notes.csv) (teaching notes for the planted cases). The column names
follow ADaM where they can, so a read-only extract with the same columns would drop in. Nothing writes
back.

## The screening rules: R/logic.R {#logic}

Every line of the rules. `hys_screen()` carries the potential Hy's Law definition with its timing
window and ALP option, the confirmation flag and the FDA discontinuation considerations;
`qtc_screen()` the QTcF categories; `ctcae_grade()` the v6.0 and v5.0 lab grades; `tpt_state()` and
`dlt_state()` the 3+3 rule reference; `study_signals()` the study tier; `trialmon_worklist()` and
`trialmon_rollup()` the worst-of roll-up.

```{r logic, code=readLines("../trialmon_shiny/R/logic.R")}
```

Three details carry most of the clinical weight. The Hy's Law test uses `.ge(ALT, 3)` (3-fold or greater)
while the confirmation flag uses `.gt(ALT, 3)` (above 3x), as the FDA text does. Bilirubin is tested
`.gt(BILI, 2)` only on draws from the day of an aminotransferase elevation to `window` days after it, and
every draw with ALT or AST at least 3x ULN opens its own window, so a second rise is not missed. And
`worst()` is the only roll-up: there is no weighted mean anywhere in the file, and the watch level is a
worklist row, so it reaches the tiers too.

### How the reactivity works

**Settings are one reactive.** `settings()` reads the CTCAE version, the Hy's Law window, the ALP
option and the MedDRA label, and falls back to the defaults if a box is cleared. `roll()` and `liver()`
depend on it, so changing a setting re-computes every panel.

**The study tier is the only editable state.** `study <- reactiveVal(STUDY0)` holds the study-level
indicators. The what-if writes a new level into it; reset puts the feed back.

**No flicker on open.** The level radio starts on the selected indicator's own level
(`selected = STUDY0$LEVEL[STUDY0$ID == KRI0]`), and both observers use `ignoreInit = TRUE`. Before, the
radio started on its first choice and its observer wrote that value into the first indicator as the
app opened, so a red signal briefly turned green. Two tests cover it: the radio's initial value in the
rendered UI, and that opening the app with that value changes no indicator. With the fix reverted in a
scratch copy, both fail.

**The download never touches the server's disk.** The observer on `input$dl` turns the worklist into CSV
text with `as_csv_text()`, with a first `data_source` column that labels every row synthetic, and sends it
with `session$sendCustomMessage("trialmon-download", ...)`; the handler in `DOWNLOAD_JS` wraps it in a
Blob and clicks a temporary link. The file is named `SYNTHETIC_trialmon_worklist_CTCAEv6.0.csv` (or v5.0).

## The tests

```r
Rscript sasr_monitoring_wiki/trialmon_tests/run-tests.R
```

`test-boundaries.R` checks each rule exactly at its threshold and just either side: ALT exactly 3x ULN,
bilirubin exactly 2x ULN, the 30-day window, a second aminotransferase elevation that opens its own
window, ALP exactly 2x ULN and the ALP option read draw by draw, QTcF 450, 480 and 500 ms, changes of 30
and 60 ms, 1 of 3 and 1 of 6 DLTs, the CTCAE cut points that differ between v5.0 and v6.0, the eDISH axis
range (every participant drawn), and the watch level reaching the roll-up. `test-logic.R` checks where
each planted case lands in the shipped data. `test-server.R` drives the app with `shiny::testServer()`:
the initial radio state, the what-if and reset, the SAP settings, the participant packet (no NA), the
CTCAE versions in the footnotes, and the synthetic-labeled download payload; it also checks that the app
uses only Shinylive-ready packages and no `downloadHandler`.
